4:1.sourceText: Ὡς οὖν ἔγνω ὁ Κύριος ὅτι ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὅτι Ἰησοῦς πλείονας μαθητὰς ποιεῖ καὶ βαπτίζει ἢ Ἰωάνης,
4:1.targetText: When therefore the LORD knew that the Pharisees heard that Jesus makes and immerses more disciples than John,

4:2.sourceText: —καίτοιγε Ἰησοῦς αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβάπτιζεν ἀλλ’ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ,—
4:2.targetText: (though indeed Jesus Himself was not immersing, but His disciples),

4:3.sourceText: ἀφῆκεν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
4:3.targetText: He left Judea and went away again to Galilee,

4:4.sourceText: Ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρίας.
4:4.targetText: and it was necessary [for] Him to go through Samaria.

groups.note: Actual auton is the accusative subject of the infinitive under edei, realized as the whole English [for] Him subject construction. Both pinned analyses remain P-ASM. No separate Greek for preposition or additional pronoun is printed.

4:5.sourceText: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρίας λεγομένην Συχὰρ, πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ·
4:5.targetText: He comes, therefore, to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near to the place that Jacob gave to his son Joseph;

4:6.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ. ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ· ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη.
4:6.targetText: and there was there a well of Jacob. Jesus therefore having been weary from the journeying, was thus sitting on the well; it was as it were the sixth hour;

groups.note: Actual kekopiakōs is PERFECT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, V-RAP-NSM in both pinned analyses. LSV having been weary expresses the same weariness state; its English been does not make the Greek form passive or introduce a separate source copula.
Actual nominative hour noun owns the English nominal frame the ... hour; actual sixth adjective remains separately linked.

4:7.sourceText: ἔρχεται γυνὴ ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρίας ἀντλῆσαι ὕδωρ. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δός μοι πεῖν.
4:7.targetText: there comes a woman out of Samaria to draw water. Jesus says to her, “Give Me to drink”;

4:8.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεληλύθεισαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἵνα τροφὰς ἀγοράσωσιν.
4:8.targetText: for His disciples were gone away into the city that they may buy food;

4:9.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρεῖτις Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρ’ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς γυναικὸς Σαμαρείτιδος οὔσης; οὐ γὰρ συνχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρείταις.
4:9.targetText: the Samaritan woman therefore says to Him, “How do You, being a Jew, ask drink from me, being a Samaritan woman?” For Jews have no dealing with Samaritans.

groups.note: Actual feminine Samaritan designation retains N-NSF in both pinned analyses and its actual article; LSV uses it attributively with the separately linked woman noun.
Actual Samaritan designation retains N-GSF in both pinned analyses, used as the English attributive designation within the same genitive woman construction.

4:10.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι Δός μοι πεῖν, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν.
4:10.targetText: Jesus answered and said to her, “If you had known the gift of God, and who it is who is saying to you, Give Me to drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

groups.note: Actual zōn is a present active participle, V-PAP-ASN in both pinned analyses, rendered as the modifier living; it remains distinct from the actual water noun.

4:11.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε, οὔτε ἄντλημα ἔχεις καὶ τὸ φρέαρ ἐστὶν βαθύ· πόθεν οὖν ἔχεις τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν;
4:11.targetText: The woman says to Him, “Lord, You do not even have a vessel to draw with, and the well is deep; from where, then, have You the living water?

groups.note: The actual qualifier article plus zōn present active participle (V-PAP-ASN in both pinned analyses) owns living, separately from the actual water noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference/explicit subject: LSV names The woman as the speaker; pinned N1904 λέγει has an implicit subject and no corresponding woman noun here.

4:12.sourceText: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰακώβ, ὃς ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ φρέαρ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔπιεν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ θρέμματα αὐτοῦ;
4:12.targetText: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and himself drank out of it, and his sons, and his livestock?”

groups.note: Actual comparative adjective meizōn retains A-NSM-C in both pinned analyses and owns greater separately from the genitive comparison complement.
Actual genitive article, father noun and first-plural possessor jointly realize the genitive comparison complement than our father. No separately printed Greek than preposition is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή signals an expected negative answer; LSV uses an English rhetorical Are You question without a separate negative word.

4:13.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Πᾶς ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος τούτου διψήσει πάλιν·
4:13.targetText: Jesus answered and said to her, “Everyone who is drinking of this water will thirst again;

4:14.sourceText: ὃς δ’ ἂν πίῃ ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος οὗ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ δώσω αὐτῷ γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
4:14.targetText: but whoever may drink of the water that I will give him, may not thirst—throughout the age; and the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water, springing up to continuous life.”

groups.note: Actual dipsēsei13 is FUTURE ACTIVE INDICATIVE THIRD-SINGULAR (V-FAI-3S in both pinned analyses), under actual ou mē. Printed TR has subjunctive dipsēsē; LSV renders may not thirst, while this correspondence retains the actual N1904 future indicative thirst head and analysis.
Actual aiōnion retains A-ASF in both pinned analyses and is rendered continuous by LSV, separately from the actual zōēn life noun.

4:15.sourceText: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνή Κύριε, δός μοι τοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ, ἵνα μὴ διψῶ μηδὲ διέρχωμαι ἐνθάδε ἀντλεῖν.
4:15.targetText: The woman says to Him, “Lord, give me this water, that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw.”

groups.note: Actual dierchōmai is the compound dierchomai head, with V-PNS-1S in both pinned analyses, rendered come in LSV’s come-here wording; actual enthade separately owns here. The primary lexical entry directly attests the coming usage at John4:15; the complete printed TR instead has simple erchōmai. The actual compound lemma is retained rather than substituted with erchomai.

4:16.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ὕπαγε φώνησον τὸν ἄνδρα σου καὶ ἐλθὲ ἐνθάδε.
4:16.targetText: Jesus says to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here”;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference/explicit subject: LSV names Jesus; pinned N1904 has only the implicit subject of says, without an expressed Jesus token here.

4:17.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἡ γυνὴ καὶ εἶπεν Οὐκ ἔχω ἄνδρα. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καλῶς εἶπες ὅτι Ἄνδρα οὐκ ἔχω·
4:17.targetText: the woman answered and said, “I do not have a husband.” Jesus says to her, “Well did you say—I do not have a husband;

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted answer after you say; LSV uses direct speech with no separate English that.

4:18.sourceText: πέντε γὰρ ἄνδρας ἔσχες, καὶ νῦν ὃν ἔχεις οὐκ ἔστιν σου ἀνήρ· τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἴρηκας.
4:18.targetText: for you have had five husbands, and now, he whom you have is not your husband; you have said this correctly.”

4:19.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Κύριε, θεωρῶ ὅτι προφήτης εἶ σύ.
4:19.targetText: The woman says to Him, “Lord, I perceive that You are a prophet;

4:20.sourceText: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν· καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου προσκυνεῖν δεῖ.
4:20.targetText: our fathers worshiped in this mountain, and You say that in Jerusalem is the place where it is required to worship.”

4:21.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πίστευέ μοι, γύναι, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ Πατρί.
4:21.targetText: Jesus says to her, “Woman, believe Me, that there comes an hour when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, will you worship the Father;

4:22.sourceText: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·
4:22.targetText: you worship what you have not known; we worship what we have known, because salvation is of the Jews;

4:23.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν, ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ Πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ· καὶ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν·
4:23.targetText: but there comes an hour, and it now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father also seeks such to worship Him;

groups.note: Actual alēthinoi retains A-NPM in both pinned analyses, separately linked from the worshipers noun.

4:24.sourceText: Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεός, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δεῖ προσκυνεῖν.
4:24.targetText: God [is] Spirit, and those worshiping Him should worship in spirit and truth.”

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV marks a supplied copula; Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεός is a Greek verbless clause.
Source witness difference/explicit object: LSV includes Him after worshiping; N1904 has no corresponding object pronoun with τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας here.

4:25.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Οἶδα ὅτι Μεσσίας ἔρχεται, ὁ λεγόμενος Χριστός· ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα.
4:25.targetText: The woman says to Him, “I have known that Messiah comes, who is called Christ, when that One may come, He will tell us all things”;

4:26.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι, ὁ λαλῶν σοι.
4:26.targetText: Jesus says to her, “I who am speaking to you am [He].”

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies the bracketed predicate after I am; N1904 has no separate He pronoun at that point.

4:27.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν Τί ζητεῖς ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετ’ αὐτῆς;
4:27.targetText: And on this came His disciples, and were wondering that He was speaking with a woman, no one, however, said, “What do You seek?” Or “Why do You speak with her?”

4:28.sourceText: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις
4:28.targetText: The woman then left her water-jug and went away into the city, and says to the men,

4:29.sourceText: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός;
4:29.targetText: “Come, see a Man who told me all things—as many as I did; is this the Christ?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μήτι introduces a tentative question (can this be?/surely not?); LSV uses a direct is this question with no separate particle word.

4:30.sourceText: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν.
4:30.targetText: They went forth therefore out of the city, and were coming to Him.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes therefore, corresponding to οὖν in the TR reading; the pinned N1904 verse has no conjunction at this point.

4:31.sourceText: Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Ῥαββεί, φάγε.
4:31.targetText: And in the meanwhile His disciples were asking Him, saying, “Rabbi, eat”;

groups.note: Actual article plus disciples noun is the whole nominal phrase rendered His disciples. LSV identifies their owner in this immediate asking-Him scene; neither pinned N1904 nor the complete printed TR has a separate possessive pronoun in this noun phrase. The article alone is not mapped to His.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV has And, reflecting a δέ connective in the TR reading; pinned N1904 begins Ἐν τῷ μεταξύ with no corresponding connective.

4:32.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.
4:32.targetText: and He said to them, “I have food to eat that you have not known.”

4:33.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν;
4:33.targetText: The disciples then said to one another, “Did anyone bring Him anything to eat?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks an expected negative answer in the Greek question; English Did anyone has no separate negative particle.

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies an object of eat for idiomatic English; N1904 has only the infinitive φαγεῖν (to eat), without an anything pronoun.

4:34.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον.
4:34.targetText: Jesus says to them, “My food is that I may do the will of Him who sent Me, and may finish His work;

4:35.sourceText: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται; ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας, ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν. ἤδη
4:35.targetText: do not say that it is yet four months, and the harvest comes; behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the fields, that they are white to harvest already.

unmappedSource.reason: LSV does not separately express the explicit Greek subject ὑμεῖς (you) in do not say. N1904 presents a rhetorical do you not say? question; the displayed LSV wording reads as a prohibition without a question mark.

4:36.sourceText: ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.
4:36.targetText: And he who is reaping receives a reward, and gathers fruit to continuous life, that both he who is sowing and he who is reaping may rejoice together;

groups.note: Actual aiōnion retains A-ASF in both pinned analyses and is rendered continuous by LSV, separately from the actual zōēn life noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins And, reflecting an extra conjunction in the TR reading; pinned N1904 begins the reaper clause with ὁ directly.

4:37.sourceText: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων.
4:37.targetText: for in this the saying is the true one, that one is the sower and another the reaper.

4:38.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.
4:38.targetText: I sent you to reap on that which you have not labored; others labored, and you have entered into their labor.”

4:39.sourceText: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα.
4:39.targetText: And many from that city believed in Him, of the Samaritans, because of the word of the woman testifying, “He told me all things—as many as I did.”

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted testimony; LSV uses direct speech with no separate English that.

4:40.sourceText: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρεῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρ’ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.
4:40.targetText: When, then, the Samaritans came to Him, they were asking Him to remain with them, and He remained there two days;

4:41.sourceText: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ,
4:41.targetText: and many more believed because of His word,

4:42.sourceText: τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ Σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου.
4:42.targetText: and said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of your speaking; for we ourselves have heard and known that this is truly the Savior of the world—the Christ.”

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted speech after said; LSV uses direct speech with no separate English that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV explicitly adds the Christ to the Savior title; pinned N1904 John 4:42 ends of the world with no Χριστός token.

4:43.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
4:43.targetText: And after the two days He went forth from there, and went away to Galilee,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV has an additional coordinated went-away clause; pinned N1904 has no καὶ ἀπῆλθεν clause here, proceeding from went forth from there to Galilee.

4:44.sourceText: αὐτὸς γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι προφήτης ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι τιμὴν οὐκ ἔχει.
4:44.targetText: for Jesus Himself testified that a prophet will not have honor in his own country;

groups.note: Actual idiāi is the A-DSF adjective in both pinned analyses, rendered his own within the same country phrase; no separately printed autos pronoun is claimed.
N1904 ἔχει is present-tense has; LSV uses will have in this negative proverbial statement. The linked phrase shares the have/hold lexeme without asserting the same tense.

4:45.sourceText: ὅτε οὖν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐδέξαντο αὐτὸν οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι, πάντα ἑωρακότες ὅσα ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ· καὶ αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν.
4:45.targetText: when then, He came to Galilee, the Galileans received Him, having seen all things that He did in Jerusalem in the celebration—for they also went to the celebration.

4:46.sourceText: Ἦλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον. Καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ·
4:46.targetText: Jesus came, therefore, again to Cana of Galilee, where He made the water wine, and there was a certain attendant, whose son was ailing in Capernaum,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference/explicit subject: LSV names Jesus as the subject of came; pinned N1904 has only an implicit subject in Ἦλθεν, with no Jesus noun here.

4:47.sourceText: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν· ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνήσκειν.
4:47.targetText: he, having heard that Jesus comes out of Judea to Galilee, went away to Him, and was asking Him that He may come down and may heal his son, for he was about to die.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: the complete printed TR adds auton after the asking predicate, reflected by LSV Him here. Pinned N1904 ērota has no separately printed object at that point; the earlier pros auton occurrence retains its own to Him correspondence.

4:48.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε.
4:48.targetText: Jesus then said to him, “If you may not see signs and wonders, you will not believe.”

4:49.sourceText: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός Κύριε, κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου.
4:49.targetText: The attendant says to Him, “Lord, come down before my child dies”;

4:50.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πορεύου· ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ. ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐπορεύετο.
4:50.targetText: Jesus says to him, “Be going on; your son lives.” And the man believed the word that Jesus said to him, and was going on,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV has And before the man believed; N1904 begins the belief clause directly with ἐπίστευσεν, without a conjunction.

4:51.sourceText: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ ζῇ.
4:51.targetText: and he now going down, his servants met him, and told, saying, “Your child lives”;

groups.note: Actual article plus servants noun is the whole nominal phrase rendered his servants under the immediately described man going down and being met. N1904 prints no separate possessor after servants, while the complete printed TR adds autou there. No additional N1904 pronoun is invented or assigned to the article alone.

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the servants speech; LSV uses a direct quotation with no separate that.

Source witness/person difference: N1904 αὐτοῦ is third-person his in the indirect report, while LSV Your follows the second-person σου of the TR direct-speech reading. No exact pronoun identity is asserted.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes an additional told clause before saying; N1904 has only λέγοντες (saying), with no corresponding ἀπήγγειλαν verb.
